name: BRIGHT
description: Benchmarks Reasoning-Intensive Generative High-quality Text Retrieval — the first retrieval benchmark requiring intensive reasoning rather than keyword or semantic overlap. Questions are drawn from StackExchange, LeetCode, and similar sources where the relevance between a query and its gold document requires multi-step reasoning to establish. State-of-the-art retrievers that score 59.0 nDCG@10 on BEIR achieve only 18.3 on BRIGHT.
typical_sota_score: ~25–35 nDCG@10 (state-of-the-art retrieval + reranking; human performance much higher)
reputation: Published at ICLR 2025; from XLang Lab (Yale), Princeton, and Google; highlights fundamental gap between semantic similarity and reasoning-based retrieval; widely cited in RAG and retrieval research
notes: Published at ICLR 2025. BRIGHT exposes that retrieval models trained on semantic similarity completely fail when relevance requires reasoning. A document may be the correct answer but share no lexical or semantic overlap with the query — the connection requires following a chain of logic. Covers 12 domains from diverse StackExchange communities, LeetCode, and similar technical sources.
